properties.digitized_from: Draft EIR Figure 2-2, "Project Site Sub-Areas and Ownership" (Potrero Power Station Mixed-Use Development Project Draft EIR, Case No. 2017-011878ENV, October 2018, p. 2-6), which shows the Port-owned "Port sub-area" (SF Port ownership, ~2.9 acres total in 3 non-contiguous pieces) at true scale with a north arrow and a 400-ft scale bar.
properties.digitization_method: Georeferenced by matching one high-confidence real-world corner (the Illinois St / 22nd St property corner, matched to this project's own fetched data.raw/parcels.geojson block 4175 boundary vertex at lon -122.387166171, lat 37.757917868) plus the figure's printed scale bar, assuming north-up with no rotation. CORRECTED 2026-09-13: the original scale-bar reading (400 ft measured at 516 px = 0.7752 ft/px) placed this polygon's centroid essentially on top of the real Sophie Maxwell Building address on Maryland St -- geographically implausible for a bay-side open space parcel, and flagged as wrong by direct user review. Re-derived the scale independently via OpenStreetMap Overpass API ground truth (real distance 934.7 ft between the 22nd St/Illinois St and 23rd St/Illinois St intersections, measured at 733 px between the same two intersections in the source figure) = 1.2752 ft/px, ~1.64x the original reading. CLIPPED TO REAL SHORELINE 2026-09-13: the rescaled convex-hull trace was a 6.4-acre pointed/diamond shape that visibly didn't follow the real waterfront's curve (flagged by the user) and overshot the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece by 4x -- a size error the rescale introduced and this project failed to re-check at the time. Clipped the traced polygon against the real Port jurisdiction boundary (data/raw/port_jurisdiction.geojson, via src/block_fit.py's clip_to_jurisdiction()), which traces the actual property/water line -- the same real-boundary-fitting approach block_fit.py already applies to streets, applied here to the shoreline. DE-SPIKED 2026-09-13: the raw clip left a ~90m thin spike where the hand-traced land-side edge grazed a real kink in the jurisdiction boundary at a shallow angle -- confirmed against real satellite imagery (ESRI World Imagery) that no real point of land exists there, just a straight riprap shoreline. Rather than hand-edit that one vertex, generalized clip_to_jurisdiction() itself to apply a morphological opening (erode 10m, dilate 10m back, in EPSG:3857) after the intersection, which erases any sliver narrower than ~20m while leaving the real boundary-following edge untouched -- a fix to the shared tool, not a one-off patch, so any future shoreline clip gets the same spike protection. Final shape simplified (tolerance 0.00003 deg) to 10 vertices, 1.56 acres -- within a few percent of the EIR's ~1.6 acres.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE ONLY -- digitized from an illustrative planning figure, not a surveyed record, then clipped to the real Port jurisdiction boundary on its water-facing side and opened to remove a spike artifact (see digitization_method). The corrected centroid falls east of the real Sophie Maxwell and UCSF Block 2 parcels, consistent with a bay-side location, and area now closely matches the EIR's stated ~1.6 acres for this piece. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly tens of meters on the land-facing sides (still convex-hull-smoothed over the true shape there), but the water-facing edge is now a real boundary, not hand-traced. Do not use for anything requiring exact boundaries.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: This land has no Assessor's Block/Lot number at all -- confirmed directly in the same Draft EIR, footnote 1, p. 2-5: "The Port sub-area, and City sub-area described below, are not assessed properties, and therefore do not have assigned Assessor's Block numbers." It therefore cannot appear in DataSF's Parcels - Active and Retired dataset and cannot be joined via status.csv/blklot.
properties.regulatory_context: Prequel Park is the ~2-acre interim open-space project (BCDC Application 2019.006.02, a non-material amendment issued June 19, 2025; SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18, 2025, amending Lease L-16662 with California Barrel Company LLC) of which ~0.4 acres sits on this Port sub-area land near the future recreational dock. Construction targeted Q3 2026, public opening targeted Q3 2027 per the Port's Nov 14 2025 memo (Calendar Item 10A).
properties.notes: Approximate polygon representing the Port-owned bay-side open-space parcel (not the precise ~0.4-acre interim-improvement footprint within it, which would require a second, compounding approximation from the Port's own non-scaled Exhibit 1 rendering).

properties.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 (shoreline shown as 'Waterfront Park'); SF Port Commission Nov 2025 memo and Spring 2026 development-forecast listing for 'Potrero Power Station - Prequel Park' (2-acre interim waterfront park).
properties.digitization_method: NEWLY ADDED 2026-09-16 -- user pointed out that the already-tracked 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' polygon (0.4 acres, near the pier's point/breakwater) should connect to Blocks 4 and 9 and to Humboldt Street Plaza, and should not overlap Block 9. That file's own regulatory_context already noted it covers only ~0.4 of a ~2-acre 'Prequel Park' interim open-space project (SF Port Commission Resolution 25-70, Nov 18 2025, amending Lease L-16662) -- the other ~1.6 acres sits on Potrero Power Station's own land (not Port jurisdiction), which had never been separately tracked. A construction-pipeline document (Spring 2026 dev forecast) independently describes this same project as a '2-acre Waterfront Park', strongly suggesting this Power-Station-land portion is the same physical shoreline corridor already traced (less precisely, and for a different purpose) as this dataset's separate 'Waterfront Park' feature (a D4D-diagram-labeled, long-term planning feature, sourced and georeferenced completely differently). Built this connector polygon by combining two already-validated sources rather than re-tracing from scratch: (1) the WEST/inner edge uses Block 4, Humboldt Street Plaza, and Block 9's own already-committed corners directly, so it shares an exact boundary with all three and cannot overlap Block 9 by construction; (2) the EAST/shoreline edge reuses Waterfront Park's own previously satellite-color-validated outer-shoreline trace (see that file's digitization_method for how it was built) between Block 4's latitude and Prequel Park (Port sub-area)'s own northernmost point, where the two pieces meet and touch -- except for a ~20m notch in that trace (its own vertices between the point at lon -122.38137/lat 37.75663 and the point at lon -122.38137/lat 37.75629) that pre-dated Block 9's GDAL/TPS correction and dipped into Block 9's real footprint; dropped those points since the west-edge chain now defines that boundary directly.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this polygon combines two different sourcing methods (see digitization_method) and has not been independently re-verified as a whole against satellite imagery. Its west edge is exact (shared vertices with Block 4/Humboldt Street Plaza/Block 9). Its east/shoreline edge inherits whatever accuracy Waterfront Park's own trace has -- treat it as a reasonable but not freshly-verified approximation of the real shoreline. This is the 'Power Station sub-area' complement to 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- together they approximate the full ~2-acre interim park project, though the true internal boundary between Port and Power-Station land has not been independently confirmed.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site.
properties.regulatory_context: The Potrero Power Station-land portion of the ~2-acre Prequel Park interim open-space project (see 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' for the Port-jurisdiction portion and its own sourcing). Construction per the Spring 2026 SF development-pipeline forecast (developer: FIFTH SPACE); scope includes demolition/site clearing, earthwork and grading, underground utilities, stormwater treatment, and landscaping.
properties.notes: Newly added 2026-09-16 to complement 'Prequel Park (Port sub-area)' -- see accuracy_caveat.

properties.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-17 a long chain of diagram/prose-based approximations (kept below for history) -- see digitization_method. Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, p.7/11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility"; (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
properties.digitization_method: REFIT 2026-09-13 with src/block_fit.py, on top of two prior corrections. (1) THIS PROJECT'S OWN real Building 12 anchor was wrong: status.csv had Building 12 joined to blklot 4045017 (700 Illinois St), an unrelated residential condo building over 500m from the real Building 12 -- corrected to 1070 Maryland St, blklot 4114010; see status.csv. (2) After correcting the anchor, this polygon (and Elevation Sky Park) was placed as a hand-computed offset rectangle, and a user screenshot showed it still crossing a real street -- the hand-computed street setbacks were not reliable. Replaced with a repeatable tool instead of a third hand computation: src/fetch_streets.py fetches real OSM street centerlines for the whole project area once (cached to data/raw/streets.geojson), and src/block_fit.py polygonizes them (plus the Port jurisdiction boundary, for shoreline-bounded blocks) into real block polygons, then fits a box of the requested size inside the correct one -- checked programmatically against every nearby street, not eyeballed. This building's real block (Maryland/21st/22nd St, the same one Elevation Sky Park occupies) is a real, well-formed small block, so block_fit.py fit it at its full documented 101ft x 75ft size, no shrinking needed, in the southern part of that block (nearer Building 12/22nd St); Elevation Sky Park occupies the rest of the same block to its north/east. ROTATED 2026-09-13: block_fit.py's earlier version always produced a true-north-aligned box, which looked visibly wrong once rendered -- this area's real street grid (Maryland/Louisiana/Delaware St etc.) is rotated relative to true north, and an axis-aligned box in a rotated block wastes space and doesn't match its neighbors' orientation. fit_box now rotates the box to match the bearing of the nearest real street segment before fitting/shrinking it. OVERLAP NOTE 2026-09-14 (project-wide overlap audit, SUPERSEDED 2026-09-16, see below): Fully overlapped Pier 70 Parcel E2 at the time -- expected given this marker's own low-confidence, directional-only placement; not clipped, since doing so would erase the marker entirely rather than usefully correct it. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 deep pass, after applying Potrero's GCP-validation lessons to Pier 70's own transform): rather than continue relying on block_fit.py's street-polygon-fit approach (which only guarantees this box sits somewhere inside the right real block, not at a source-verified position), went back to the same source diagram used for this site's numbered parcels -- Figure 6.4.2 (Building Height Maximum), which shows Building 21 directly as one of its labeled gray 'Historic Buildings' boxes -- and pixel-traced its box directly (programmatic pixel-color sampling to find the box's true edges, at x=1551-1651, y=833-909 in the 2376x1836px source image, after an initial visual estimate proved off by ~55-60px on a badly-scaled crop). Converted via this site's validated 6-point affine transform (the same one used for Parcels A-H, residual error 1-8m against 5 real street intersections plus Building 12's real Assessor centroid) -- NOT block_fit.py's separate street-polygonize method. Cross-checked the transform itself against Building 12's real centroid (blklot 4114010) before trusting this result, per the lesson learned from Potrero's mis-measured-GCP incident: the transform reproduces Building 12's real-world position acceptably well, so it is not grossly miscalibrated. RESULT (2026-09-16, later superseded -- see below): this diagram-derived position was initially found to overlap Pier 70 Parcel E1 by 429.8 m2. FALSE ALARM, RESOLVED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass, later same day): a user-flagged visual check found E1's own traced shape was badly wrong (a misshapen quadrilateral that cut through this very '21' box and the open space beyond it, rather than the real L-shaped 90ft/65ft footprint shown on Figure 6.4.2). E1 was re-traced programmatically from its own two legend colors -- see pier70_e1.geojson's digitization_method -- and the overlap with this file dropped to exactly 0 m2, confirming Building 21's own position here was correct all along; the earlier overlap was entirely an artifact of E1's bad shape. Still overlapped 'Elevation Sky Park' by 275 m2 (unaffected by the E1 fix) -- see accuracy_caveat. RESOLVED 2026-09-17: that separate ESP entry was merged into Pier 70 Parcel E3's own row per an explicit user decision (see pier70_e3.geojson) and is no longer plotted as its own block, so this overlap no longer applies -- kept here for history. UPGRADED TO REAL FOOTPRINT 2026-09-17 (user request: 'building 21 can be more precise by leveraging satellite image, since it's an existing building that will remain'): rather than keep tracing/re-fitting a hand-drawn box, searched DataSF's Building Footprints dataset for real structures near this site (mblr=SF4052001 -- the same giant, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot found to underlie much of central Pier 70, also covering Building 14; see status.csv's 4052001 row) and rendered all of them directly over ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. That rendering showed two real, adjacent dark-roofed structures (367.8 and 367.2 sq m, combined 734.96 sq m / ~7,911 sqft) sitting almost exactly under this file's own previously-committed diagram-derived box -- a close match (within 4.4%) to the previously-cited 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) footprint size. A third, larger nearby footprint (1,879.7 sq m) that a pure diagram-position guess had initially favored turned out, on the satellite image, to actually be a paved section of Maryland St itself (a street mistakenly captured as a 'building' in the source dataset) -- not a structure at all; ruled out once seen against real imagery, exactly the kind of error satellite cross-checking is meant to catch. A small adjacent 49 sq m footprint sits ~9m south of the two main pieces (not touching) -- possibly a small appendage or a separate utility structure; not confirmed, so not included. Replaced the hand-traced diagram box with the union of the two matched real footprints (MultiPolygon, since DataSF's extraction has them as two separate touching-but-unmerged pieces). Checked for overlap against E1, E3, E4, Parcel D, Building 2, and Building 12's real parcel -- zero overlap with all of them at this corrected, smaller, more precisely-positioned footprint.
properties.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) as of 2026-09-17 -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 21: position matches multiple independent prose sources (adjacent to Building 12, fronting Slipways Commons) and its combined size (734.96 sq m) is within 4.4% of the previously-cited 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) documented footprint. The match rests on position, size, and satellite corroboration, not an explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there). A small 49 sq m footprint ~9m away was not included -- see digitization_method. Superseded history: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-13 -- this building's rehabilitation has not started as of the most recent primary sources found (see regulatory_context).
properties.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and sits on the same huge, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot (blklot 4052001) as Building 14 and other structures across central Pier 70 -- no distinct blklot exists to join for Building 21 specifically, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually (see digitization_method).
properties.regulatory_context: Building 21, originally Substation No. 5, was relocated on-site and is one of three historic structures (with Buildings 2 and 12) the Pier 70 Design for Development commits to rehabilitating per the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (Pier 70 D4D S6.6.1). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row marked it "complete," inferred (not directly cited) from Building 21 being grouped in the D4D's rehabilitation commitment alongside Buildings 2 and 12. A follow-up research pass found the Port's own 28-acre site page (sfport.com/projects-programs/pier-70-28-acre-site) describes Building 21's rehabilitation as still to come -- the page shows a rendering, not a photo, captioned "Rendering of Pier 70 Building 21," under a "Rehabilitation of three historic buildings" heading, implying a future vision rather than a completed project. This is corroborated negatively by the Port's own June 2025 project-update deck (sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/Pier%2070%20Update%20-%20June%202025%20v3.pdf), which documents Building 12 and Building 15's full rehabilitation histories in detail but never mentions Building 21 having been touched. Status corrected from complete to existing (see status.csv for this value's definition) -- a standing historic structure, not yet rehabbed, with no confirmed construction timeline.
properties.notes: UPGRADED 2026-09-17 to a real, surveyed building footprint (was a hand-traced diagram box) per user request -- see digitization_method. Building identity and footprint are now both well-confirmed.

properties.digitized_from: Mission Rock Design Controls (Port of San Francisco / Mission Rock Partners, adopted April 24, 2018), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151); land use from Figure 1.1 - Land Use Plan (p.10); block corners snapped to the recorded DataSF Assessor lot lines of the 2020 Seawall Lot 337 subdivision where they fall within 3 m.
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Mission Rock Design Controls' own Figure 6.2 (Maximum Height Plan, p.151) -- an adopted regulatory diagram with a printed scale bar and street grid, not an illustrative rendering. Georeferenced using 5 real street-intersection control points (3rd St x Channel St, 3rd St x Long Bridge St, 3rd St x Mission Rock St, Bridgeview Way x Mission Rock St, Terry A. Francois Blvd x Mission Rock St), fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py and matched to their pixel positions in the diagram, then fit as a least-squares affine transform (never fewer than 5 points spanning the whole site, not just 1-2 nearby anchors). Cross-validated against the diagram's own printed scale bar and against the real, independently-confirmed positions of Verde, The Canyon, Building B, and Visa HQ (Building G) -- all four fell inside their correct named blocks under this transform, which is what caught and fixed an earlier, much worse-fitting 4-point version of this same transform (a block letter read one row off, producing 75m of error) before it was used for anything. Residual error against the 5 control points is roughly 3-13m. RETRACED 2026-09-17 (brief docs/briefs/mission-rock-geometry.md; definition of done in docs/site-definition-of-done.md). (1) SOURCE. This file's source_doc_urls pointed at the March 2012 'Design + Development Revised Proposal' (90 pages, no Figure 6.2) while the text cited the Design Controls, so the original pixel measurements could not be reproduced. Redone from the adopted Mission Rock Design Controls (April 24, 2018, sfport.com), Figure 6.2 - Maximum Height Plan (p.151), rendered ONCE at 300 dpi to data/manual/_reference/mission_rock_dc_p151.png (3300x2550 px, full page). Every pixel measurement below is from that one render. (2) TRANSFORM (one for the whole figure). Since this file was first traced, the Assessor subdivided Seawall Lot 337 (recorded 2020-06-12, mapped 2021-04-13): the four Phase 1 blocks are real lots -- A/The Canyon 8719B002, G/Visa 8719A008, B 8719C003, F/Verde 8719C001 -- whose recorded areas match the plan's block areas within 3%. The figure's drawn corners of A, B, F and G (colour contours, OpenCV) were matched to those 16 real lot corners and a least-squares affine transform fitted: RMS residual 0.67 m, worst corner 1.39 m (n=16); scale 0.2570 m/px (x) and 0.2598 m/px (y), ratio 0.989; axis angle 89.88 deg, i.e. no shear. The figure's own printed 200 ft scale bar measures 239 px on the same render = 0.255 m/px, agreeing within 2%. lon = 2.9127666757282e-06*px + 2.2156884853242e-07*py + (-122.39479060102); lat = 1.6823215817497e-07*px + -2.3273617315092e-06*py + 37.77752553008. (3) VALIDATION on real lines NOT used in the fit: traced C and D west corners fall 0.2-2.4 m from the 3rd Street property line (west edge of the undivided remainder lot 8719A006); D and H south corners 0.1-1.5 m from the Mission Rock Street property line (south edge of 8719A006); J, I and H east corners 1.1-2.8 m from the Terry A Francois Boulevard property line (east edge of 8719A006 / west edge of the TAFB lot 8719A003); the traced Block K corners fall 0.7-1.3 m from the corners of the lobe of the park lot 8719A005 that K occupies. Bearing check, the shear test that Pier 70's point check missed: real 3rd St property line 355.6 deg vs figure 355.3; real TAFB property line 355.7 vs figure 356.1; DataSF Exposition Street (Toni Stone Crossing) centerline 85.7 deg vs the figure's Exposition axis 84.9 deg, with 0.2 m offset at mid-block. (4) METHOD. Each block's fill (base colour plus hatched upper-building zone) was isolated by colour saturation inside a pixel window, its outer contour extracted and simplified (approxPolyDP, 1% of perimeter), transformed, and then any vertex within 3 m of a recorded lot line of 8719A006, 8719A003, 8719A005, 8719A007, 8719A009, 8719A010, 8719C001, 8719C002, 8719C004 or 8719D001 was snapped onto that line, so street frontages and shared edges are the Assessor's lines rather than the figure's 1-3 m of contour noise. Cross-checked against an independent trace of the same block on Figure 1.1 (p.10) through its own transform fitted the same way (RMS 1.1 m). (5) CHECKER. Registered in src/verify_block_fill.py under site 'mission_rock' (pixel window and colour rule recorded there); CI prints the IoU against the figure's own fill on every run. C SPECIFICS: 4 vertices; 3 vertex(es) on lot 8719A006, 1 vertex(es) on lot 8719C004; area 39,190 sf vs 40,208 sf in the March 2012 Revised Proposal's parcel table (-2.5%); the north edge is the south lot line of Channel Street (lot 8719C004), the west edge the 3rd Street property line.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE (planned, unbuilt block): no Assessor lot of its own yet. It sits on lot 8719A006, the ~37,400 m2 undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 that also holds Blocks C, D, E, H, I, J, Mission Rock Square, Channel Lane and the unbuilt internal streets. Traced 2026-09-17 from the adopted Design Controls' Figure 6.2 through a transform with 0.7 m RMS residual on 16 real lot corners, with vertices snapped to recorded lot lines where the figure draws the block against one (see digitization_method): treat street-facing and lot-line edges as accurate to ~1 m and interior edges (against unbuilt streets and open spaces) to ~1-3 m. The block's shape is the Design Controls' block, not a building footprint; a building may sit back from these lines.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor lot exists under this block -- 8719A006, the undivided remainder of Seawall Lot 337 recorded 2020-06-12 -- but it has not been subdivided per block, so joining status.csv to it would paint the same ~9-acre parking-lot shape for every unbuilt block. Hand-derived geometry is used instead, with the lot's own lines wherever this block touches them.
properties.regulatory_context: Commercial Mixed Use only (no residential option) per the D4D's Land Use Plan (Figure 1.1) -- ground-floor retail required. Max building height 190 ft per Figure 6.2, confirmed exactly. Positioned south of Block B, fronting 3rd St to the west and the Shared Public Way (and Mission Rock Square beyond it) to the east. No construction-start source found -- still surface parking as of the most recent research pass (Sept 2026).
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted future block -- not yet built, no distinct real parcel yet. See accuracy_caveat.

properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17. China Basin Park (the Design Controls' name; 'Mission Rock Park' in the 2012 proposal) opened April 2024 with Phase 1 (sfyimby.com, 2024-04-26). Its real Assessor lot is 8719A005: 18,975 m2 / 4.69 ac, created when Seawall Lot 337 was subdivided in 2020. The lot has not been split, so this feature is the recorded lot geometry (223 vertices, simplified to 2e-7 deg / ~2 cm) minus that lobe, cut exactly along the lobe's recorded north line so the park and Block K touch with no gap; a 99 m2 sliver left along the paseo lot line by the cut was dropped. Area 186,359 sf (4.28 ac) vs 204,246 sf for the whole lot; the Design Controls and Phase 1 submittal describe the park as ~5 acres, the 2012 parcel table as 5.12 ac including Block K's frontage. OpenStreetMap's park polygon (way 27656676, 19,480 m2) has IoU 0.76 with the whole lot and also includes the K lobe; the recorded lot is used as the higher-authority boundary, per the definition of done. Routed through approximate_projects.csv rather than status.csv (like Crane Cove Park and the Pier 70 building footprints) only because the K lobe had to be carved out; if the Assessor splits Block K off, replace this file with a status.csv row on the park's new lot.

Channel Wharf is the paved waterfront plaza between Piers 48 and 50, east of Terry A Francois Boulevard, at the end of the Channel Street / Square / Channel Lane axis. The 2020 subdivision gave the TAFB right-of-way lot 8719A003 a rectangular notch there -- north edge shared with the Pier 48 lot 8719A001, east edge 27 m out at the wharf face, south edge on Pier 50's north line -- so the polygon is that notch, using the lots' own four recorded vertices (21,142 sf, 0.49 ac). Cross-check: IoU 0.65 against the green Channel Wharf fill traced independently on Figure 1.1 through its own transform (RMS 1.1 m); the figure's fill runs a few metres further east over the water edge than the lot line does, and its west edge is drawn at the TAFB shared zone rather than the lot line, which explains the difference. Not registered in verify_block_fill.py (no fill on Figure 6.2).
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE but high confidence: all four edges are recorded DataSF lot lines (the notch of lot 8719A003), agreeing with the Design Controls figures to within a few metres. Planned, unbuilt open space; the notch is a working wharf / staging area today.

properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): re-measured programmatically instead of by eye, for consistency with the rest of this site -- isolated this legend color (RGB [128,193,219]) and extracted a clean rectangular contour (OpenCV) at pixel (1203,437)-(1401,682). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Result is close to (within ~5m of) the prior hand-read version -- this parcel's own corners were already read correctly; kept for methodological consistency across the site. Still overlaps 'Noonan Building' by ~2843 m2 -- an already-documented, expected overlap given Noonan's own low-confidence, directional-only placement.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (fifth pass): user-flagged check found this block's boundary itself (not a clipping artifact) was missing an entire row of real, currently-used parking near 20th St -- the diagram-derived north edge sat ~25m south of the lot's actual northern extent. Measured directly against satellite imagery (same method as the west-edge fixes on B/E1/E2) and moved the north edge to the real curb/crosswalk line at 20th St. CORRECTED AGAIN 2026-09-14 (seventh pass): user clarified the diagonal row of angled cars along this block's west side is curbside parking on Illinois Street itself, not part of the PKN/PKS parcel -- the earlier fixes had mistakenly extended the west edge to include it. Pulled the west edge back east to -122.3874, matching where the diagonal on-street parking row ends and the lot's own perpendicular-grid parking begins (visually distinct in the satellite image). CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (eighth pass): auditing this block for the same curb-vs-lot-line mistake found and fixed on Pier 70 Building 2 (see that file's digitization_method, failure mode 6 in src/bearing_trace.py), a user-flagged review found the north edge (set in the fifth pass above) still had exactly that bug -- it was anchored on the 20th St curb/crosswalk line, one row of real angled parking too far north. That front row runs at a different angle than the rest of the lot's parking, has no visible separation from the street/crosswalk itself (i.e. it reads as curbside street parking, not a lot with its own frontage), and is set off from the second (and subsequent) rows by a real gap with a visible pavement-color change -- the same 'significant white separation' signal already used to exclude curbside parking on this block's west edge. Re-anchored the north edge at that second-row transition (approx. lon -122.38695, lat 37.76041) using this site's established grid bearing and line_intersection(). This moved the north edge roughly 7-8m south of the fifth-pass version. THIS WAS WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (ninth pass): user clarified the eighth pass misread the imagery -- the diagonal row immediately south of the street IS part of PKN's own lot (it shares the same angle and spacing as the rest of the lot's parking), not curbside street parking. What actually sits between the street and that row is a much thinner sliver -- a single line of vehicles parked facing a DIFFERENT direction (parallel to the curb, not angled into the lot) -- that thin sliver, not the whole first diagonal row, is the real on-street parking to exclude, and it has no visible delimitation from the street itself (matching the earlier west-edge lesson: on-street parking reads as part of the street, not the lot). Re-measured the true boundary at the top edge of the diagonal row (where the angled spaces actually begin, immediately past that thin curbside sliver and the street's own paved width): lon -122.38696, lat 37.76061 -- essentially the SAME position as the fifth-pass version (within ~1m), confirming the fifth pass had already found the right line and the eighth pass's 'fix' was a real regression, not a correction. Lesson generalized in src/bearing_trace.py: when applying the curbside-parking-exclusion pattern, check the EXCLUDED band's own vehicle orientation and depth before assuming a whole matching row is street parking -- a thin, differently-angled sliver right at the curb is the real signal, not simply 'the row closest to the street.' STILL WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (tenth pass): the ninth-pass fix anchored the whole north edge on a SINGLE measured point (at the west end) plus the site's established perpendicular bearing (86.5 degrees), rather than this specific edge's own two-point bearing -- exactly the shortcut this project's own bearing_trace.py methodology warns against (derive an edge's bearing from that edge's own two endpoints, not a borrowed one), and it produced a line that hugged the real row's top edge correctly at the west end but drifted north into the gap above the row by the east end. User annotated two separate crops (west portion and east end near the building corner) showing the true row-top edge; extracted the marked line's actual pixel path in both images and converted to real coordinates (rather than eyeballing), giving two well-separated points -- (-122.38702427, 37.76055681) and (-122.38675117, 37.76056792) -- 24m apart. Their own bearing (87.06 degrees) is close to the established 86.5 (confirms the site bearing was never the problem) but using these two real points directly, rather than one point plus an assumed bearing, fixed the drift: the resulting edge now hugs the row's top consistently at both ends, confirmed by zooming into each end separately after the fix. STILL WRONG, CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (eleventh pass): user pointed out the tenth-pass line still cut through a visible sidewalk -- a clearly lighter, more uniform-toned paved band sitting between the excluded curbside sliver and the real diagonal parking, distinct in color/texture from the lot's own darker, worn pavement. Confirmed quantitatively: averaging pixel brightness in bands parallel to the tenth-pass line (canceling out individual-car noise) showed a bright, ~3.5m-deep band immediately south of that line before brightness dropped off into the lot's own darker pavement -- i.e. the tenth-pass line sat inside the sidewalk, not at its far edge. Moved the edge 3.65m further south (same bearing, both endpoints shifted equally) to the point where the bright band ends and the lot's own pavement begins. Overlay-confirmed at both ends: a clearly lighter band is now visible between the old and new lines, and the new line sits right at the top of the real parking row with no sidewalk-toned pavement above it. TWELFTH PASS, same day (west/east edges): user asked to apply the same color-based criteria to the west and east edges, which had not been re-audited since their much earlier fixes. West edge: found the committed line ran straight through a second, distinct column of diagonal parking, splitting it in half -- there is a real walkway/gap west of that column (between it and the truly-curbside first column along Illinois St), and the whole second column sits on the PKN side of that walkway. Moved the west edge (both NW and SW, same bearing, parallel shift) 5.27m further west to that walkway, confirmed by zooming into both a wide view and a close-up: the previously-split column is now fully included and the true curbside-only column stays excluded. East edge: initially over-corrected by expanding 5.5m east, based on a large open paved apron that had similar color/texture to the lot -- user caught this: a curving driveway edge visible at the south end of that same apron indicates it's a road/driveway curve, not more lot, despite the matching pavement color. Reverted the east edge (NE, SE) back to its prior, un-expanded position -- ground color alone was not sufficient here without also reading the shape of the boundary (a curving edge is a strong road/driveway signal that overrides a same-color match). REVERTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): the twelve satellite-imagery-driven passes above were built on a mistaken premise -- this project maps the D4D's PLANNED layout (including streets and open space not yet built) against today's satellite imagery as a backdrop, not the other way around. Snapping this parcel's boundary to today's real parking-lot striping was wrong: it silently deleted 'Public Open Space' shown directly on Figure 6.4.2 (a green strip between this block and 20th St) and erased '21ST ST (NEW)' entirely, a real, deliberately-labeled future street the diagram draws with its own paved width between PKN and PKS. Re-traced this block directly from Figure 6.4.2 instead: programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating this legend color, RGB [169,143,173]) found this block's own purple fill spans pixel x 420-665, y 475-787 in the 2376x1836 source image (y=475 is where the fill begins, south of the green open-space strip; y=787 is this block's south edge, north of 21ST ST (NEW)'s own ~35px/~20m-wide drawn width) -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform used for this site's other numbered parcels. This restores the diagram's own street and open-space gaps that the satellite-snapping passes had collapsed to zero. The satellite-based lessons above (curbside-parking exclusion, sidewalk-color detection, driveway-curve reading) remain useful technique notes for tracing REAL/existing features elsewhere in this project, but do not apply to this PLANNED parcel's own boundary. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review, prompted by a user request to audit street alignment sitewide): the pixel measurement immediately above ('x 420-665, y 475-787') was taken from a 2376x1836-resolution copy of Figure 6.4.2, but was then run through this site's 6-point affine transform, which was calibrated against the 2200x1700-resolution page171.png -- a resolution mismatch that silently shifted this whole block by the 2376/2200 = 1.08x scale factor (the same class of bug independently found and fixed on Building 21's old trace). Cross-checked against the neighboring blocks this touches: the corrected PKN-PKS gap (21st St NEW) is now 15.4m (previously reported as 19-26m under the old, larger trace -- both are plausible street widths, but 15.4m is what the corrected geometry actually gives), and this fix also required correcting the '20th Street Plaza' frontage strip (data/manual/pier70_pkn_frontage_plaza.geojson), which had explicitly copied this block's old (wrong) x-range and south-edge y-value -- see that file's own digitization_method. Traced this strip's bounding box directly: pixel x 420-665 (matching PKN's own east-west extent exactly, so this shares an exact boundary with PKN and cannot overlap it), y 401-475 (from the site's own Project Site Boundary line at 20th St down to where PKN's own building fill begins). CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review): both pixel values above ('x 420-665', 'y...475') were inherited directly from PKN's own 2376x1836-resolution measurement, which turned out to have been run through the 2200x1700-calibrated affine transform unrescaled -- a confirmed bug (see pier70_pkn.geojson's digitization_method) that also mismeasured PKN's east edge independent of the scale error. Since this plaza was defined to share PKN's exact x-range by construction, it inherited both problems. Corrected to match PKN's newly-retraced, correct-resolution contour exactly: x 389-578 (PKN's real east-west extent), y 371-440 (440 = PKN's corrected north edge, matched exactly so the shared boundary still can't overlap; 371 = 401/1.08, rescaling the south-boundary-line pixel reading since it comes from Figure 3.3.1, not 6.4.2, and there is no independent legend-color fill to re-detect there). EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'tiny and divided by the road'): join_approximate.py's automatic real-street clip was silently discarding ~69% of this feature (leaving a ~384 sq m sliver of the traced ~1,255 sq m, and splitting it into disconnected fragments where the real street's buffer cut through it) -- which is exactly what 'tiny and divided by the road' looks like. This strip's whole purpose (per Figure 3.3.1) is to replace part of TODAY's wider real 20th Street with tomorrow's narrower street + landscaped frontage -- the same 'the diagram's plan overrides today's satellite imagery' principle already hard-won on PKN itself (see that file's own extensive revert history, where satellite-snapping this exact frontage was tried and explicitly reverted for the same reason). Real curb data here doesn't cleanly separate 'street' from 'lot' anyway (this whole area is currently one undifferentiated surface parking lot, same ambiguity documented on PKS before its own unrelated positioning bug was found). Set street_clip_exempt so this feature renders at its full traced size against the real, planned frontage depth Figure 3.3.1 shows, rather than being cut down to whatever survives clipping against a street this plan is meant to narrow. REVERSED 2026-09-17, SAME DAY (user-flagged: 'not on 20th street? Should be south of 20th'): wrong call -- checked where this polygon's north edge actually sits relative to the real 20th St centerline (not just the buffer) and found it extends 70-95m PAST the centerline, onto the north side of 20th Street entirely (into the block containing Buildings 102/104), not just a modest planned narrowing of the near curb. Available real depth here is thin (4-6m, similar to PKN's own south-edge finding against 21st St) -- resulting area is ~305 sq m, much smaller than the original ~1,255 sq m illustrative-bbox trace. properties.project_name: Pier 70 Waterfront Open Space (Waterfront Terrace / Slipways Commons / Waterfront Promenade / Pier 70 Shoreline) -- combined, approximate
properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named/numbered per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52).
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass): the D4D names four separate open spaces along this site's waterfront -- Waterfront Terrace (Fig 3.4.1 zone 1, near Parcel B), Slipways Commons (zone 2, the plaza between E1/E4 and E2/E3), Waterfront Promenade (zone 3, the shoreline path), and Pier 70 Shoreline (zone 4, near the point north of E4) -- but Figure 3.4.1 itself (and Figure 6.4.2's own 'Public Open Space' fill, used here) renders all four as ONE continuous, undivided green area with no internal boundary line drawn anywhere between them. Rather than fabricate a specific dividing line that no source shows, this is tracked as one combined feature covering all four. Traced via programmatic pixel-color detection (isolating Figure 6.4.2's 'Public Open Space' fill color, RGB [194,218,106], with morphological closing to bridge small text/icon gaps, then an OpenCV contour extraction simplified to ~35 vertices) rather than hand-clicking, since this is a long, irregularly-shaped (and intentionally jagged/riprap-shore-like, per the diagram's own hatching) strip. Converted via this site's validated 6-point affine transform. Clipped against Parcels E1, E4, E3, and H2's own already-committed geometries via shapely difference() (the raw pixel trace overlapped each by a small amount, and building parcels take priority over this open-space trace) -- this produced a MultiPolygon with one large piece (~3.0 acres) and a smaller ~0.23-acre piece separated by H2. NOT clipped against Building 21 or Elevation Sky Park (this site's own already-acknowledged low-confidence markers) for the same reason those aren't clipped against E1-E4 elsewhere in this dataset. GAP FILLED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): a ~31m gap existed directly east of Parcel E3 -- this polygon's two pieces each nearly touched E3 near its NW and SW corners (per the earlier clip against E1/E4/E3/H2) but nothing filled the shoreline strip along E3's own east edge in between, even though Figure 6.4.2 shows this whole shoreline band as one continuous Public Open Space area with no break at E3. Added a connecting piece along E3's east edge, bounded on the east by the real Port Jurisdiction boundary (data/raw/port_jurisdiction.geojson, the same authoritative shoreline/bulkhead line already used elsewhere in this project) rather than an invented shoreline shape, and clipped against E3's current (2026-09-17, extended-south) geometry so it doesn't overlap it.

Total traced area (~4.0-4.3 acres before/after clipping) is a reasonable match to the D4D's own combined figures (a ~5.0-acre waterfront area covering the first three, plus part of a ~1,300-linear-foot shoreline) but is not a precise subdivision or survey. properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 systematic feature-by-feature pass); REDONE 2026-09-17 (first pass) after a user-reported visual bug (this plaza appeared to render as a thin diagonal ribbon crossing Maryland St into the E2/H1 area, nowhere near Building 12) -- traced from the diagram's own green pixel fill, clipped tightly against Building 2/D/12, producing a conservative ~0.35-acre result. REDONE AGAIN 2026-09-17 (second pass, same day) after the user pointed out this was still wrong: the D4D drawing shows Buildings 2, D, and 12 coming together with green space to fill the ENTIRE street block (Louisiana St to Maryland St), but the diagram-pixel-clip approach left large unaccounted gaps (~17-18m strips of bare pavement between Building 2/12's real satellite-verified positions and the diagram's own, less precisely-drawn green boundary) that didn't match either the drawing's intent or satellite reality. Switched approach entirely: used this project's own src/block_fit.py (load_blocks() + find_containing_block()) to get the REAL, street-polygonized city block bounded by Louisiana St and Maryland St (the same tool used to place Elevation Sky Park and Building 21's earlier approximations), unioned it with Parcel D's own geometry (D's north edge extends slightly beyond the polygonized block, toward the not-yet-built 21st St (NEW)), then subtracted Building 2's real/satellite-corrected geometry, Parcel D's own geometry, and Building 12's real Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) via shapely difference(). This directly guarantees the block reads as fully filled -- buildings plus this plaza, no gaps -- rather than depending on how precisely the diagram's own green pixels were drawn relative to each building. Verified via a rendered satellite overlay (with an explicit PathPatch, not a naive geopandas .plot(), to confirm the resulting hole around Building 12 is real and not a plotting artifact) that the result correctly excludes both buildings and covers the rest of the block. Resulting area ~5,590 sq m (~1.38 acres), much closer to the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres than either prior attempt. Confirmed zero overlap with C1, C2, HDY1/2, E1, and PKS.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- derived from a real, street-polygonized city block (not a diagram pixel-trace), subtracting Building 2, Parcel D, and Building 12's own committed geometries. This is a deliberate departure from pure diagram-tracing: since Figure 6.4.2's own green fill didn't precisely reach the real (satellite-corrected) edges of Building 2 and Building 12, using the real block boundary instead better matches both the drawing's evident intent (this block reads as fully built-out, buildings plus plaza, no gaps) and the satellite ground truth. The block polygon's north edge stops slightly short of Parcel D's own north edge (~14m, since the not-yet-built '21st St (NEW)' isn't in real street data) -- unioned with D's own extent to avoid an artificial gap there. Area (~1.38 acres) is close to, but still a bit under, the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres for this named space -- the remaining gap most likely reflects the plaza's true extent continuing south past the mid-block passage (labeled '15' on the diagram) into the block south of Building 12, which is not part of this feature.

properties.project_name: Irish Hill Playground and Irish Hill Corner Plaza -- combined, approximate
properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52), zones 7 and 8.
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-17 in response to a user-caught gap: this project's whole open-space network for Pier 70 (Figure 3.4.1, p.52) lists 8 named zones, but only 6 had been traced -- Irish Hill Playground (zone 8, ~2.0 acres per the D4D text, 'an open space adjacent to the existing remnant of Irish Hill') and Irish Hill Corner Plaza (zone 7, no acreage given) were missing entirely. FIRST PASS: traced the green 'Public Open Space' fill (RGB [194,218,106]) directly from Figure 6.4.2's pixels, then clipped it against PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own committed geometries -- this ceded roughly 45% of the raw trace back to those neighbors and left an underestimate (~0.68 acres) that didn't visually touch several of the surrounding parcels. SECOND PASS same day: switched to the real, street-polygonized block (src/block_fit.py) bounded by Illinois St and 22nd St, unioned with PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2's own geometries, minus those same 5 parcels -- fixed the touching problem for PKS/HDY3/HDY1-2 but the user caught two remaining defects: it still had small (2.5m and 9.8m) gaps against C1 and C2 (the real street-block polygon's own edges don't line up exactly with C1/C2's independently-traced boundaries), and it incorrectly extended ~13m south of HDY1/2's own south edge (the real block reaches all the way to 22nd St's actual curb, which is slightly further south than HDY1/2's own, separately-traced south edge -- creating a sliver of 'phantom' park space south of a parcel that the diagram shows going straight to 22nd St). THIRD PASS: re-included the original diagram-traced raw contour (see first pass) in the union alongside the real block and the 5 parcels -- since that raw trace independently overlapped C1 by 1,142 sq m and C2 by 74 sq m, unioning it in extends the combined shape properly into contact with both (0m gap, confirmed) without the crude 'buffer everything outward' approach tried and rejected first (which fixed the C1/C2 gap but ballooned the total area to 3.3+ acres by reaching past C1/C2 in directions that had nothing to do with Irish Hill). Then explicitly clipped the whole result to never extend south of HDY1/2's own southernmost latitude, fixing the second defect directly rather than hoping the union wouldn't overreach. Also dropped one degenerate near-zero-area sliver piece (9e-6 sq m) left over from the boolean operations. Resulting area ~7,831 sq m (~1.94 acres). FOURTH PASS 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review): PKS and HDY3 were both re-traced this same pass after a confirmed pixel-resolution bug moved them (see those files' digitization_method) -- HDY3 shifted to stay attached, but PKS moved further away, reopening a ~23m gap between this feature and PKS. The real, street-polygonized block (from the third pass) fell just 2.6m short of the newly-corrected PKS on its own -- a small, plausible real gap between the block-polygonization tool's edge and PKS's own diagram-traced edge, not the ~23m the raw union produced -- so the block polygon (only, not the parcels) was buffered outward by 6m before unioning, closing most of it; a residual 1.26m gap remains against PKS specifically, accepted as within this project's already-documented 5-15m trace precision rather than chased further with more buffering (which was tried at 15m earlier in this file's history and caused an unrelated overreach). Re-verified 0m distance / 0 overlap against HDY3, C1, C2, and HDY1/2, and 0 overlap with PKN and the 20th Street Plaza. Dropped a new degenerate sliver piece (~12 sq m) from this pass's boolean ops. Resulting area ~10,338 sq m (~2.55 acres) -- larger than the D4D's ~2.0-acre citation, mostly from the corrected PKS/HDY3 positions genuinely opening up more real space here than the earlier (buggy, too-far-south) PKS/HDY3 traces implied; not re-shrunk to hit the citation, since the citation was never used as a target, only a plausibility check. FIFTH PASS 2026-09-17 (REPLACED, user-flagged 'Irish Hill Playground seems misplaced'): the block_fit/union approach above was abandoned entirely. Looking at the actual diagram again, this green area is not just 'whatever real block Irish Hill roughly sits near' -- Figure 6.4.2 draws its exact boundary directly, including the hill's own contour-line hatching. Re-traced it the same way Waterfront Open Space was traced: isolated the 'Public Open Space' fill color (RGB [194,218,106]) in a crop covering the PKS/HDY3/C1/C2/HDY1-2 area, morphological close+open to bridge hatching/text gaps, OpenCV contour extraction (simplified to 15 vertices), converted via the validated 6-point affine transform. This raw trace overlapped HDY3/HDY1-2/C1/C2 by small amounts (each block's own black border stroke sits a couple pixels inside where the flat green fill visually ends), so it was clipped via shapely difference() against all four of those committed geometries -- same pattern as Waterfront Open Space's own clip against E1/E4/E3/H2. While investigating the C1 overlap specifically, found C1 itself carried the same 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug already fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3 (see pier70_c1.geojson's digitization_method) -- its true south edge is ~26m further north than previously recorded, which had been silently eating into this exact area. Fixed C1 first, then re-ran this clip. Result: 0m gap/overlap against HDY3, HDY1/2, and C2; 0.9m gap against the corrected C1 (within normal trace precision); the ~23m distance to PKS is NOT a gap to close -- the diagram shows PKS separated from this open space by the full width of HDY3, they were never meant to touch. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (second pass, same day): after the shear fix above, a user-flagged visual check still showed this block overlapping paved streets. Root cause found: several blocks (PKN, PKS, HDY3, HDY1/2, E4) had their OWN corner pixel positions misread during transcription -- e.g. PKN's west edge was recorded as pixel x=163 when the diagram's own gridline labels put it at x=355 (which is where the Illinois St anchor point itself was measured). This was a transcription slip, not a transform error -- the 6-point transform's anchors were unaffected (confirmed: A, B, C1, C2, D, E1, E2, E3, F/G, H1, H2 were read correctly the first time). Re-read all 5 affected blocks' corners directly against their crop images' own labeled gridlines and recomputed. CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (third pass): user-flagged overlap between HDY3/HDY1-2 and between E2/H1 and E3/H2 -- both were transcription errors (HDY1/2's diagonal notch was oversimplified into a plain rectangle that re-overlapped HDY3; E2/E3's bottom edge was misread as the row further south, landing on top of H1/H2). Re-read against the diagram's own gridlines and confirmed zero geometric overlap with the adjacent block this time. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (Pier 70 border-alignment audit): this block's north edge (its shared internal division with PKS, not a real street) was a plain diagram-corner-misread -- two independent grid-overlay crops of Figure 6.4.2 confirmed the true PKS/HDY3 divider sits at pixel y~927-932, ~55-60px north of where this file had it (y~985-992), which had left a real gap unclaimed by either polygon. Moved this block's NW/NE corners to pixel (374,927)/(591,927) -- matching PKS's own corrected south edge exactly -- via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Also shifted the next vertex (originally a small step just south of the old NE, presumably marking where this block's east edge begins its diagonal cut toward the southern point) north by the same amount, to preserve its position relative to the corrected NE rather than leaving it stranded mid-shape. The block's own southern extent (the far-south point corner) is unchanged, unaffected by this fix. CORRECTED 2026-09-16 (second pass, same day): user-flagged visual check found the same-day fix above left a visible kink -- the un-shifted southern vertex no longer lined up with the block's true diagonal edge. Re-measured this block's ENTIRE shape programmatically instead of patching individual vertices: isolated this legend color (RGB [169,143,173]) in a fresh crop, connected-component labeled it, and extracted its precise contour (OpenCV, simplified to its 4 real corners). Result: NW(420,932), NE(591,932), a corner where the east edge turns into the diagonal cut (591,1027), and the block's own southern point (437,1195) in pixel space -- converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. This replaces both today's earlier patches with one clean, from-scratch re-measurement; confirmed zero overlap with PKS (north) and HDY1/2 (south, across the Irish Hill Playground gap). CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (streets/block-alignment review, prompted by a user request to audit street alignment sitewide): the pixel measurement above (NW/NE at y=932, from a 'fresh crop') turns out to have been taken from the same 2376x1836-resolution copy of Figure 6.4.2 that caused the confirmed resolution-mismatch bug on PKN and PKS's old traces (420*1.08=453.6... more precisely, this block's own values are exactly 1.08x this site's correct 2200x1700-resolution measurement: 932/1.08=863.0, 420/1.08=388.9, 591/1.08=547.2 -- all matching a fresh, independent re-measurement on page171.png to within 1px). Re-measured directly on page171.png: this block's true contour is (547,863)-(389,863)-(389,1107)-(404,1107)-(547,951) in pixel space (a slightly larger polygon than the old one, extending further south since the old trace's southern point (437,1195) was itself part of the same bad crop). Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed touching (0m gap, 0 overlap) with the newly-corrected PKS to the north; the ~44m gap to HDY1/2 (part of Irish Hill Playground) is preserved as before. RE-INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (yet again, same day, after user feedback called the prior revert-and-redo cycle 'mostly a downgrade' and asked for a clarifying question rather than another guess): went back to first principles instead of more pixel geometry. Two checks, both requested by the user: (1) searched the D4D's own text (Section 4.11, Specific Streets Design Intent) for any description of 21st St being relocated or realigned -- found none; it describes 21st St as 'primarily serves as an alley from Illinois Street to the waterfront,' with no mention of a moved alignment. (2) Pulled real satellite imagery (src/satellite_check.py) directly over where DataSF's official centerline (CNN 15232000/15233000) says 21st St runs between Illinois and Michigan St -- it shows vegetation, graded dirt, a tree, and a vehicle-storage yard: zero pavement. So the earlier 'the D4D relocates 21st St' theory (this file's own prior REVERTED/RETRACTED entries) was an overreach from a real but simpler fact: DataSF's centerline here is a paper (platted, unbuilt) alignment, the same failure mode as three other already-excluded CNNs in street_geometry.py (12915000, 15200000, 15228000) -- not a deliberate relocation. Added CNN 15232000/15233000 to that same exclusion list, with the satellite evidence documented there. User's explicit instruction: note that this stretch of 21st St isn't built yet, but for this map's purpose (showing the planned FUTURE parcel state) treat the diagram's own drawn '21ST ST (NEW)' position as authoritative. Restored this block to its pure diagram-transform position accordingly -- the same value already found and confirmed multiple times this project (most recently before the mistaken ground-truth shift below). Area restored to ~2,699 sq m. REPOSITIONED 2026-09-17 (user override: 'take my input as override... turn that Michigan span into 21st st and adjust parcel positioning accordingly'): re-anchored to the corrected planned 21st St line (see pier70_21st_street.geojson -- built from Michigan St's own real terminus point, perpendicular to Illinois/Louisiana's real ~175.5-degree bearing), replacing the Figure 6.4.2 pixel-traced position used previously. Also user-instructed to ensure this block borders 22nd Street directly (the D4D diagram itself only brings this block's diagonal cut close to HDY1/2's own NW corner, leaving a small Irish Hill Corner Plaza sliver between it and 22nd St -- overridden per explicit instruction). North edge (NE/NW) shifted by the same amount as the adjacent PKS corners, preserving the touching relationship. Reshaped the block's whole south/diagonal portion: extended a new west edge straight down along Illinois St's own longitude from the (shifted) NW corner to the real 22nd St curb line (6.8m north of centerline), then connected east along that same curb to the repositioned HDY1/2's own NW corner (which was, in the same pass, also extended to the real 22nd St curb -- see that file), then up along HDY1/2's own diagonal edge back to its NW corner, replacing this block's old, shorter diagonal cut entirely. This new southern extension initially overlapped the real Illinois St street buffer by 31% (a real, substantial encroachment, not a normal corner sliver) -- clipped via shapely difference() against the real-street buffer, dropping the extension's own width along Illinois St to whatever real room exists there. Final area ~2,306 sq m (the north portion carried over from the PKS-anchored shift, plus this new Illinois-frontage extension down to 22nd St). Confirmed 0 overlap with the repositioned HDY1/2 (0m gap, touching) and re-clipped Irish Hill Playground against this new shape (see that file). RECONSIDERED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: this block and HDY1/2 should keep the diagonal disconnect via Irish Hill Playground, not touch directly): tried a version with a ~12m-wide gap preserved between this block's own Illinois-St extension and HDY1/2's west edge, for Irish Hill Playground to occupy down to 22nd St. Measured the REAL available space there directly: the real street buffer (Illinois St, CNN 7169001) extends east to within 2-9m of HDY1/2's own west edge along this whole stretch (checked at 4 latitudes between 22nd St and this block's own north portion) -- there isn't real room for a separate gap-preserving corridor without either cutting into Illinois St's own right-of-way or making HDY1/2 narrower. Reverted to touching HDY1/2 directly (0m gap) at the 22nd St corner, using the 9.8m curb+sidewalk offset -- this satisfies 'borders 22nd Street' but does NOT restore the diagonal disconnect; flagged this specific tension back to the user rather than silently picking a side. REDESIGNED 2026-09-17 (two user-flagged issues, same pass): (1) 'HDY3 and PKS should have the same width' -- this block's own north edge was still only ~39m wide (its old, pre-Michigan-extension measurement) while PKS grew to ~75m wide after its own Michigan St extension. Set this block's NE corner to PKS's exact SE corner (-122.386554, 37.75906638453553), matching PKS's width exactly and closing that gap to 0m. (2) 'resolve the HDY3/HDY1-2 diagonal disconnect' -- restored a real, meaningful gap to HDY1/2 (narrowed slightly in the same pass, see that file) for Irish Hill Playground to occupy, rather than touching directly as the prior round left it. Reshaped this block's southern portion as a clean quadrilateral: NW straight down Illinois St to 22nd St curb, then east along the curb to a point 6.7m short of HDY1/2's own (narrowed) west corner, then up to a point offset from HDY1/2's own NW corner by a similar margin, closing the gap on both sides. EXEMPTED FROM STREET CLIPPING: the naive version of this new southern portion was clipped 24-31% by the real street buffer near the Illinois/22nd corner and fell ~15m short of the real 22nd St curb -- checked via satellite and found this specific corner is Illinois St's own real diagonal on-street parking apron plus a private, currently-industrial paved yard (equipment/vehicle storage), not a public thoroughfare this block would need to cross -- the same 'plan the redevelopment, not today's ad hoc site use' reasoning already applied to HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground's own Michigan St exemptions. Exempted so this block reaches 22nd Street directly, per explicit instruction, rather than being cut down by a routine clip against a same-site informal condition. CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (two more user-flagged issues, same review pass: 'HDY3 should border Illinois like PKS and PKN, in the continuity' and 'the diagonal you create between HDY3 and HDY1/2 should be made of 2 parallel edges'): (1) west-edge continuity -- this block's NW corner (v1) had never been put on the same real-Illinois-St-offset line as PKN's and PKS's own west edges (each was independently diagram/satellite-traced), leaving a several-meter 'wobble' where the three blocks' own west edges met. Recomputed all of PKN's SW corner, PKS's NW/SW corners, and this block's NW corner (v1) from one shared formula: interpolate real Illinois St's centerline (CNN 7169000) latitude at each corner's own latitude -- i.e. solve for the centerline's longitude there -- then offset 9.8m east (this project's standard curb+sidewalk allowance). This puts all three blocks' west corners exactly on one consistent line for the first time. v2 (this block's own southern extension of that same edge, down to the 22nd St corner) was shifted east by the identical delta as v1 (preserving the v1-v2 edge's own prior shape/bearing exactly) rather than independently re-solving v2 against both the Illinois and 22nd St offset lines -- that dual-offset intersection was tried first and produced a self-intersecting polygon (v2 landed east of v3, crossing the v3-v4 edge), because v3 is a fixed, judgment-call point in the same messy, exempted, real-world industrial corner (see EXEMPTED note above) and isn't itself pinned to a pure Illinois-line intersection. The applied fix keeps the polygon valid while still moving the whole west frontage onto the corrected line. (2) parallel corridor -- the gap this block leaves for Irish Hill Playground to reach HDY1/2 (v3-v4 edge) was not parallel to HDY1/2's own corresponding edge (v3-v0 in that file): bearings were 19.1 degrees vs 11.2 degrees, an 8-degree mismatch, visibly not a clean corridor on the map. Fixed by keeping v3 fixed (the 22nd St curb attachment) and this edge's own prior length (86.1m) unchanged, but rotating it to HDY1/2's own v3-v0 bearing (11.2 degrees, since that block's corners are more directly tied to established real-street offsets) -- confirmed the perpendicular gap between the two lines is now uniform (~17.0m) at both ends, i.e. genuinely parallel, versus varying before. Re-validated: polygon is simple/non-self-intersecting, 0 overlap with PKS and HDY1/2 (touching PKS with 0m gap as before). REBUILT 2026-09-17 (user-flagged, third time: 'HYD3 is too messed up' -- sent an unlabeled version of the map and asked to draw a replacement by hand): the formula-driven approach above, while internally consistent, produced a shape the user judged wrong on sight. User hand-drew both HDY3 and HDY1/2 directly on the unlabeled satellite map (out/pier70_unlabeled.png) and asked for their sketch to be used as the baseline, cleaned up for parallelism. Digitized their drawing: (1) matched the user's uploaded photo (a resized/JPEG-compressed crop) back to the exact source render via ORB feature matching against the unmodified basemap content (393/419 inlier keypoints, near-pure similarity transform -- scale 2.069x, negligible rotation/shear), confirming precisely where their crop sits in the full render's pixel space; (2) independently calibrated that full render's own pixel<->lon/lat mapping by re-rendering it with small marker dots at known vertices (this project's own already-committed HDY3/HDY1-2 corners) and detecting their pixel centers -- sub-pixel (<0.6px) residuals confirmed the fit; (3) isolated the user's hand-drawn lines by color (a bright saturated blue distinct from this map's own semi-transparent parcel fills) and extracted each shape's corners. Cross-checked the pipeline by transforming the user's drawn NE corner (which should coincide with the real, already-fixed HDY3/PKS shared corner) and found it landed within ~7m of that known point -- confirming the geo-registration itself, with the residual being ordinary hand-drawing imprecision. Final shape: NE corner kept exactly at the existing HDY3/PKS shared point (unchanged); NW corner snapped exactly onto PKS's own SW corner (the user's drawn point independently landed within ~2m of it, confirming their sketch already preserves the Illinois St continuity fixed earlier the same day) rather than the previous 22nd-St/Illinois-intersection formula; SW (22nd St) corner taken directly from the user's drawn point; corridor edge (facing HDY1/2) rotated to exactly match HDY1/2's own corresponding edge bearing (see that file) while preserving the user's own drawn edge length, keeping the corridor genuinely parallel (uniform ~17m gap) as requested. Re-clipped Irish Hill Playground against this new shape (322 sq m new overlap, since this shape reaches further into that space than the previous round's -- see that file). 0 overlap with PKS (unchanged shared edge) and HDY1/2 (17m corridor gap, confirmed parallel).
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). RE-TRACED 2026-09-17 directly from Figure 6.4.2 at the correct source resolution (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment. SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged): this block's north edge had drifted 1.26m south of PKS's own south edge (both blocks were independently re-measured at different times and no longer shared an exact boundary, despite the diagram showing them as one continuous fill with only an internal divider line). Snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's south-edge coordinates exactly, closing the gap to 0m. RE-SNAPPED 2026-09-17 (same day): PKS itself was found to be badly mispositioned (60% of its area was being silently clipped away against the real 21st St -- see pier70_pks.geojson) and was shifted ~25m south to ground-truth against the real street. Re-snapped this block's NW/NE corners to PKS's new south edge to stay attached; area dropped from ~2,699 to ~1,508 sq m as a direct, expected consequence of PKS moving into what was previously this block's own north portion. This block's own south/diagonal portion (touching HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground) is unchanged. INVESTIGATED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'HYD3 too small relative to its peers based on drawing'): checked whether this shrinkage is a real bug (i.e., whether the same northward transform bias found on PKS/C1/PKN/Building 113-116 also affects this block's own south/diagonal portion, which would justify shifting HDY1/2 and Irish Hill Playground south too, restoring this block's diagram-implied size while keeping everything attached). Tested this directly: interpolated the real, official 22nd St centerline's latitude at HDY1/2's own south-edge longitudes (the nearest independently-checkable real street to this cluster) and compared to HDY1/2's current south edge -- found a clean ~14m gap with NO overlap, unlike PKS's 60% real-street overlap that justified its own correction. This is the opposite signature from a 'drawn too far north' bug: if the same bias reached this far south, HDY1/2 would itself be overlapping 22nd St, not comfortably clear of it. Conclusion: the 21st-St-row bias is local to that row and does not extend to this block's own south portion or to HDY1/2/Irish Hill Playground -- there is no evidence basis to shift them south to recover this block's pre-fix size. This block's current, smaller size is treated as the accurate, forced consequence of ground-truthing PKS (which shares this block's own north edge), not an unresolved bug. Flagging this conclusion explicitly per this project's no-fabrication rule: if a future source shows this block's own south/diagonal corners were independently misread (a diagram-reading error, not a bias-correction consequence), that would still warrant revisiting this specific block on its own.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Residential per Brookfield's leasing brochure (not 'parking support' as sometimes described secondhand), 65 ft max per Figure 6.4.2 (a uniform height, not a 40-65 ft range). Named for the former PG&E 'Hoedown Yard' that once occupied this area. Shown as a separate parcel from HDY1/2 in the D4D's own figure. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.

CORRECTED 2026-09-17 (found by src/verify_block_fill.py, a new reusable diagram-fit checker built after user feedback that too much of this project's QA was one-off pixel investigation that's easy to get subtly wrong and hard to redo consistently): this block was never rechecked for the 2376x1836-vs-2200x1700 resolution-mismatch bug independently found and fixed on PKN/PKS/HDY3/C1/Building 21 on 2026-09-17 -- it slipped through because that day's fixes were driven by individual user-flagged visual checks, not a systematic re-verification of every block.
